world_org_meetings.title: In UN address, Anand takes jab at 'great powers' disrupting global order
world_org_meetings.description: Foreign Affairs Minister Anita Anand has put "strategic autonomy" at the forefront of Canada's address to the United Nations General Assembly today.

world_org_meetings.title: Former U.S. Ambassador to Israel on Netanyahu's speech at UNGA
world_org_meetings.description: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks with former U.S. Ambassador to Israel Thomas Nides about Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech at the United Nations General Assembly.

world_org_meetings.title: Pope in Paris, Xi in DC, AI at a Crossroads
world_org_meetings.description: It’s been a week of walkouts, power plays and diplomatic theatre — from a battle over press freedom in Washington, to a United Nations General Assembly marked by protests and departures, as leaders clashed over Iran, Cuba and Venezuela. There was also a rare red-carpet meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, as the US and China extended their trade truce and turned their attention to the race for dominance in artificial intelligence. And from the geopolitical to the spiritual, Pope Leo brought his call for restraint and regulation of AI to France, as he sought to position the Vatican as a moral voice in a rapidly changing world.

world_org_meetings.title: Actors Susan Sarandon, Hannah Einbinder among detained protesters outside Netanyahu's UN speech
world_org_meetings.description: Actors Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder were among the protestors detained in New York City on Thursday as Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a speech to the United Nations General Assembly.

world_org_meetings.title: Zelenskyy addresses UN as Rubio of U.S. says Ukraine, Russia have interest in limited ceasefire
world_org_meetings.description: Russia pounded Kyiv with drone strikes on Wednesday, hitting railway infrastructure, warehouses and fuel stations, just hours before Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy addressed the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

diplomatic_visits.title: Trump offered to sell arms to China during Xi visit, US ambassador tells Fox News
diplomatic_visits.description: The United States is required by law to supply Taiwan, which has a democratically elected president and legislature, with weapons for its defence under the 1979 Taiwan Relations Act.

diplomatic_visits.title: UAE confirms Israel PM Netanyahu’s visit to Abu Dhabi
diplomatic_visits.description: The visit took place as the Israeli prime minister battles domestic turmoil ahead of October's Knesset elections.

diplomatic_visits.title: REPLAY: France's Macron speaks on European Union as pope visits Metz
diplomatic_visits.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said that Europe must rediscover the “courage of its founders” and not give in to the “resurgence of nationalism" as he delivered an address alongside Pope Leo XIV in Metz on the last day of the pontiff's visit to France.

diplomatic_visits.title: Trump gave Xi Jinping a warm welcome. What did the talks accomplish?
diplomatic_visits.description: From the National Archives to the state dinner, President Trump and Xi Jinping looked comfortable together in Washington. Two former NPR China correspondents on what the visit did and didn't deliver.

diplomatic_visits.title: The week in pictures: Trump hosts Xi, the pope visits France and floods ravage Thailand
diplomatic_visits.description: From Pope Leo XIV's historic first visit to France to US President Donald Trump meeting China's President Xi Jinping to flooded streets in Bangkok, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.

elections.title: Vucic resigns as Serbia's president, setting up election that could see him become PM
elections.description: Serbia's populist president, Aleksandar Vucic, resigned on Sunday to pursue a bid to become the prime minister in an upcoming early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country after nearly two years of protests.

elections.title: French student protests fuel political clash ahead of 2027 Presidential vote
elections.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon traded barbs on Monday over high school students blockading classes to demand more resources. The students cite teacher shortages, deteriorating schools and heavy schedules. The dispute comes ahead of next spring’s presidential election, amid mounting pressure over France’s finances.

elections.title: French far-right's Bardella denies alleged 2013 antisemitic comments as Le Pen sees boost in polls
elections.description: A French investigative website on Monday alleged that far-right National Rally leader Jordan Bardella made antisemitic comments in writing in 2013, but the close ally of presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen dismissed the claims as fake. The allegations emerged as Le Pen's prospects for the 2027 elections appear stronger than at any point in her previous campaigns. FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin speaks with Dr Andrew Smith, Lecturer in History and Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London.

elections.title: Israel's opposition bloc, Netanyahu’s coalition in dead heat, election poll finds
elections.description: With a month to go until Israel goes to the polls on October 27th, a new opinion poll shows the opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party in a dead heat with Prime Minister Benyamin Netanyahu's coalition. It comes as the leaders of the four main opposition parties pledged to work together.

elections.title: As midterms approach, does GOP have a Trump problem?
elections.description: The US midterm elections are just five weeks away - and while the US President is not on the ballot, his influence is top of mind for Republicans. Donald Trump's approval ratings have been hitting record lows in recent weeks, and in a sign of the party's concern it has started pouring campaign funding into many seats once considered safe, and some candidates have even changed their tune on one of the election's biggest issues: The US's war in Iran.
